title: Context-aware prefetch admission and bandwidth-aware graceful-trim playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: implement a context-aware admission controller that combines selective prefetching of hot KV/prefixes with bandwidth-aware request admission and graceful-trim degradation modes to preserve SLOs during regional load spikes and multi-region failovers.

Background: during past regional failovers and sudden tenant hotspots we observed cascading latency increases caused by cache-miss amplification and large inflight requests. Existing token-bucket admission plus priority lanes reduce overload, but clients experiencing cold-KV misses or slow network tails still push long-running requests onto the slow path causing SLO violations for higher-priority lanes.

Proposed approach:
- Admission gate evaluates incoming request against: tenant priority band, token budget, per-tenant recent cache-hit-rate, and cross-region tail-latency signal.
- If a request is likely to trigger expensive cold-KV or large decode work, controller will: (a) opportunistically perform a background prefetch of prefixes/KV (best-effort), and (b) probabilistically admit a slimmed request (graceful-trim) that truncates non-critical continuations or reduces sampling/beam width.
- Bandwidth-aware shaping: incorporate egress bandwidth headroom into admission decisions (counts against a per-shard bandwidth credit) so we avoid saturating inter-region links during failover.
- Circuit sentinel: a lightweight circuit-breaker watches request amplification (cache-miss->latency) and can temporarily elevate conservative trimming policies or reject low-priority requests.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Prefetching increases read load and may cause short-term bandwidth spikes; strategy uses capped concurrency and LRU eviction of background prefetch tokens.
- Graceful trimming changes output fidelity; must be transparent to clients via structured-response metadata and documented fallbacks in Console.
- Complexity added to admission decision path; must remain sub-ms for common fast-path decisions.

SLO targets:
- Maintain P95 generation latency <= 220ms for P0/P1 tenants under 1.5x baseline traffic with one region degraded.
- Limit introduced background-prefetch bandwidth to <= 10% of shard egress by default (configurable).

P95 for P1 tenants improved by ~12% when prefetch successfully warmed KV hits; worst-case trimming reduced tail latency but reduced mean tokens generated by 8% for trimmed requests.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc signed off by Reliability and SRE
Unit and integration tests covering admission logic, prefetch LRU behavior, and bandwidth-credit accounting
Operator-facing Console controls: per-tenant prefetch budget, global prefetch enable/disable, and trimming aggressiveness slider
Grafana dashboards showing prefetch hit-rate, egress credit utilization, admission rejections, and trimmed-response fraction
Chaos/Blast-radius test demonstrating SLO preservation (P95 <= target) under simulated regional failover with configuration variations
Runbook update describing detection, mitigation, and rollback steps for prefetch-driven overloads
Migration plan and feature flag rollout: dark launch, canary (5% traffic), widen to 25%, then 100% with metrics gates
implementation_notes: Admission evaluation must be written in the fast-path; use precomputed lightweight signals (recent hit-rate, egress-credits, tenant-priority) to avoid heap allocations.
Background prefetch worker runs outside main request thread with backpressure; expose per-shard concurrency semaphore.
Graceful-trim modes implemented as request transformations rather than model config flips so we can preserve the same runtime path and metrics.
Circuit sentinel should emit structured telemetry events so the Console can build alert rules tied to surge and prefetch amplification.
Feature flag gating: runtime/flags/prefetch_admission_v1; Console should be able to toggle trimming aggressiveness at runtime.
